newsitem.title: USA: Telebras extends gains in rebound.
newsitem.headline: Telebras extends gains in rebound.

text.p: Telebras ADRs extended their gains Wednesday afternoon after rebounding from a sharp decline the previous day.

American Depositary Receipts of Telecomunicacoes Brasileiras SA -- the Brazilian state-run telephone holding company known as Telebras -- were up 7-11/16 to 142-5/16 by late afternoon. Trading was heavier than average at 3.35 million shares, placing the issue among the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.

Telebras, Brazil's bellwether stock, fell 11-1/4 Tuesday, after climbing to a record 169-1/4 last Thursday. Brazilian markets were shaken by concerns that Brazil would follow several Asian countries that have devalued their currencies.

Telebras "is the cheapest stock in the Latin American telecoms, but the (recent) price rise far outpaced any conceivable earnings gains," said Alfredo Jollon, a Latin American telecommunications analyst for Lazard Freres. "It was easy come, easy go."
The rise also came after reformist President Fernando Henrique Cardoso won approval of a law allowing Telebras to be privatized. The bill was signed into law earlier Wednesday.
Robert Fleming Securities analysts William Laurent and Ronald Aitken reiterated their buy rating on Telebras. They remained confident about Brazil's fundamentals.
